headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because ChatGPT Desktop can read local/app content and Prefect can broadly egress workflow metadata.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported macOS app content, so malicious content could reach it through shared artifacts. Prefect itself is not shown ingesting ChatGPT output by default, so the pairwise injection path is indirect rather than guaranteed. The interaction is plausible but not proven to be a default bridge.
conditions: IF Prefect workflows ingest ChatGPT-generated text from files or copied output without sanitization, injection risk becomes active.
IF the operator uses clipboard or shared files as the bridge between the agents, attacker-controlled content can propagate.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Use a read-only staging file for any ChatGPT output.
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes generated text.
Strip instructions and markup from imported content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Prefect has broad network egress and handles workflow metadata. If ChatGPT outputs sensitive content into a workflow artifact, Prefect can transmit it onward. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is a default-possible but not certain leakage path.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop is given sensitive files or screenshots and its output is written into Prefect-managed workflow metadata, leakage risk is active.
IF Prefect sends workflow metadata to external services, any embedded sensitive content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in ChatGPT inputs.
Redact sensitive fields before passing artifacts to Prefect.
Restrict Prefect workflows to non-sensitive metadata.
Review outbound destinations for Prefect runs.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on workflow payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it has limited direct write conflict with Prefect. Prefect's profile also does not show local filesystem write or git mutation. With no overlapping mutable resource exposed, only a small coordination risk remains.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to mutate a shared repository or directory outside the shown profile, write conflict risk increases.
IF another orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT Desktop in read-only review mode.
Run Prefect against isolated workflow copies.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Use explicit file locks for any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate code, summaries, and app-context outputs that Prefect could consume as workflow metadata or automation input. Prefect is an orchestrator, so if it treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream pipeline actions. Verification is not documented in the profiles, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Prefect uses ChatGPT-produced text as a task spec or parameter without validation, cascading error risk is active.
IF downstream Prefect tasks trigger external side effects based on that text, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human approval before Prefect executes generated instructions.
Validate all ChatGPT outputs against a schema.
Limit Prefect tasks to idempotent dry runs first.
Log and diff generated parameters before execution.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between generation and orchestration.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Prefect is described as handling workflow metadata only. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and retention surfaces, so a small compliance gap is plausible. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair's data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ChatGPT Desktop and then copied into Prefect workflow metadata, compliance scope expands.
IF Prefect retention exceeds the operator's policy for the same data class, a mismatch exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Classify workflow metadata before ingestion.
Set short retention on Prefect artifacts.
Document allowed data classes for ChatGPT Desktop.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across the pair.
